note: Each column of Quantinuum's published emulator parameter table (Emulator_parameters.csv, repository quantinuum-hardware-specifications at 59e68bb) mapped to selene-sim 0.3.8. Meanings from the repository's qtm_spec/combined_analysis.py emulator_parameters() (read as text, not run) and Quantinuum's Emulator Noise Model documentation page (docs-quantinuum/noise_model.txt). 'selene_depolarizing' is Selene's own DepolarizingErrorModel; 'selene_plugin' is our error-model plugin (plugin/rust/lib.rs) loaded through Selene's documented error-model plugin interface (selene_core.ErrorModel, a shared library built against selene-core 0.3.4 from the selene-sim-v0.3.8 tag).

selene_0_3_8_error_models.DepolarizingErrorModel: p_1q, p_2q, p_meas (one figure for 0 and 1), p_init; a uniform Pauli on each rxy and rz (1q) and rzz and rpp (2q) native operation, placed before the operation; no leakage, memory or crosstalk
selene_0_3_8_error_models.SimpleLeakageErrorModel: p_leak per operation and leak_measurement_bias; leakage spreads to the partner of any two-qubit gate; no Pauli noise. One error model per run, so it cannot be combined with the depolarizing model
selene_0_3_8_error_models.plugin_interface: an error model is a shared library (C ABI, exported with selene_core's export_error_model_plugin!) that receives every batch of native operations with the runtime's start time and duration, and has full access to the simulator (gates, measurement, reset). This is what makes leakage, asymmetric readout, measurement crosstalk and a clock-based memory term expressible
selene_0_3_8_error_models.runtimes: SimpleRuntime (rz is a native operation) and SoftRZRuntime (rz is a frame change folded into later rxy phases; no rz reaches the error model; operations of a type are batched as soon as their qubits are free; per-type durations set the batch clock). All runs here use SoftRZRuntime with duration_ns_rzz = 1 and every other duration 0, so the clock counts layers of two-qubit gates

p1.selene_plugin: fault after every rxy native operation with probability p1; rz is a frame change and carries none, as on the device
p1.match: probability exact; channel approximate: Quantinuum's is 'asymmetric depolarizing' with weights it does not publish, Selene's is X, Y, Z evenly

p1_emission_ratio.meaning: fraction of p1 faults that are spontaneous emission; an emission applies X a quarter of the time, Y a quarter, leakage half (documentation)
p1_emission_ratio.selene_plugin: as stated; a leaked qubit takes no gates, reads as 1, returns on reset, and is traced out of the state when it leaks
p1_emission_ratio.match: plugin: as documented, except that what an H2 emulator does with a leaked qubit is not published (the documentation says its leakage model, with seepage, is in the Helios emulators and not the H2 ones)

p2.meaning: 2-qubit fault probability of the fully entangling ZZ gate
p2.selene_plugin: fault after every rzz with probability p2, at any angle
p2.match: exact at the fully entangling angle; not representable from the table: the angle scaling (przz_a to przz_d, przz_power), which the table does not give, so every smaller-angle rzz is charged the full p2 (the application's model scales it on a line from 0.24 p2 at zero angle)

p2_emission_ratio.meaning: fraction of p2 faults that are spontaneous emission on one qubit of the pair
p2_emission_ratio.selene_plugin: a fault is an emission on one qubit, chosen evenly, with this probability; otherwise one of the 15 two-qubit Paulis evenly
p2_emission_ratio.match: plugin: as documented; whether an H2 emulator draws the emission once per gate or per qubit is not published; the partner of a leaked qubit in a later two-qubit gate gets I, X, Y or Z evenly (our assumption)

dephasing_error.meaning: memory (transport) RB error per memory step, a one-qubit gate included
dephasing_error.selene_plugin: Z with probability 1.5 (dephasing_error - p1) per clock unit (one layer of two-qubit gates, as the runtime schedules them) while a qubit holds a state a Z can change, charged when the qubit is next used
dephasing_error.match: approximate: Quantinuum's emulator applies linear and coherent quadratic dephasing over the durations of its own transport schedule; the table gives neither the rates nor the durations. The placement (one step per qubit per two-qubit layer) is the application's own

p_crosstalk_meas.meaning: crosstalk fault probability per mid-circuit measurement, which 'effectively measures other qubits in the trap or cause them to leak' (documentation)
p_crosstalk_meas.selene_plugin: each measurement measures every other qubit in use with probability p and discards the result
p_crosstalk_meas.match: plugin: the measuring branch only; the split between measuring and leaking is not published

p_crosstalk_init.selene_plugin: supported; the table is blank for every H2 row, so 0

not_in_the_table.p_init: no column; 0 in both models (the application's model charges a reset as a readout, an assumption)
not_in_the_table.angle scaling, quadratic and coherent de: not published in the table; not used

selene_structure.mid-circuit measurement: Guppy's project_z is a measurement, a fresh qubit and an X if the bit read was 1: a readout error therefore also flips the qubit afterwards, and the X is one more rxy with its p1 fault. It does not change a trace that is already wrong
selene_structure.zero-angle and pi-angle rzz: dropped and made a frame change (rz(pi) on each qubit) respectively, as the application's model treats them (frame_only_rzz); 1 to 187 zero-angle rzz in each chemistry circuit, 1,198 in the 12
selene_structure.compilation: Guppy's Classical level: every gate as written, nothing merged; the circuits are the package builder's gate lists, SHA-256 equal to vendor/results/circuits/manifest_sha256.json
